verses.saheeh: O you who covers himself [with a garment],
verses.khattab: O you covered up ˹in your clothes˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿O you enveloped in your mantle, the Prophet (s) (al-muddaththir is actually al-mutadaththir, but the tā’ has been assimilated with the dāl) that is to say, the one who is enwrapped in his clothes when the Revelation [Gabriel] comes down on him,
verses.romanUrdu: Aey oad lapeit (enveloped) kar laitney waley

verses.saheeh: Arise and warn
verses.khattab: Arise and warn ˹all˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿arise and warn: threaten the people of Mecca with [punishment in] the Fire should they refuse to believe;
verses.romanUrdu: Utho aur khabardar karo

verses.saheeh: And your Lord glorify
verses.khattab: Revere your Lord ˹alone˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and magnify your Lord, exalt [Him] above what is ascribed [to Him] by the idolaters;
verses.romanUrdu: Aur apne Rubb ki badayi ka elan karo

verses.saheeh: And your clothing purify
verses.khattab: Purify your garments
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and purify your clothes, from impurity, or [it means] shorten them, instead of [imitating] the way in which the Arabs [are wont to] let their robes drag [behind them], out of vanity, for perhaps they will be sullied by some impurity;
verses.romanUrdu: Aur apne kapde paak rakho

verses.saheeh: And uncleanliness avoid
verses.khattab: ˹Continue to˺ shun idols
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and shun [all] defilement, [this rijz] was explained by the Prophet (s) to be the graven images; in other words, persist in shunning them.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur gandagi se dur raho

verses.saheeh: And do not confer favor to acquire more
verses.khattab: Do not do a favour expecting more ˹in return˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And do not grant a favour seeking greater gain (read tastakthiru as a circumstantial qualifier) in other words, do not give something in order to demand more in return: this [stipulation] is specific to the Prophet (s), since he is enjoined to [adopt] the fairest traits and the noblest of manners;
verses.romanUrdu: Aur ehsan na karo zyada hasil karne keliye

verses.saheeh: But for your Lord be patient.
verses.khattab: And persevere for ˹the sake of˺ your Lord
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and endure patiently for the sake of your Lord, [all His] commands and prohibitions.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur apne Rubb ki khatir sabr karo

verses.saheeh: And when the trumpet is blown,
verses.khattab: ˹For˺ when the Trumpet will be sounded
verses.jalalayn: ﻿For when the trumpet is sounded, when the trumpet is blown, that is, the Horn (qarn), at the second blast,
verses.romanUrdu: Accha jab soor mein phook maari jayegi

verses.saheeh: That Day will be a difficult day
verses.khattab: that will ˹truly˺ be a difficult Day—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿that day, that is to say, the time of the sounding (yawma’idhin is a substitution for the preceding subject, and is not declined because it is annexed to something that cannot be declined; the predicate of the subject [is the following]) will be a harsh day (idhā is operated by what is indicated by the statement: ishtadda’l-amru, ‘[for when the trumpet is sounded] the situation will be terrible’),
verses.romanUrdu: Woh din bada hi sakht din hoga

verses.saheeh: For the disbelievers - not easy.
verses.khattab: far from easy for the disbelievers
verses.jalalayn: ﻿for the disbelievers, not at all easy: herein is an indication that it will be easy for believers despite its harshness.
verses.romanUrdu: Kafiron ke liye halka na hoga

verses.saheeh: Leave Me with the one I created alone
verses.khattab: And leave to me ˹O Prophet˺ the one I created all by Myself
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Leave Me [to deal] with him whom I created (wa-man khalaqtu is a supplement to the direct object, or [it is] an object of accompaniment) lonely (wahīdan is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the man, ‘whom’, or to the pronoun referring to it but omitted from khalaqtu [sc. khalaqtuhu]), alone, without family or wealth — this was al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī —
verses.romanUrdu: Chodh do mujhey aur us shaks ko jisey maine akela paida kiya hai

verses.saheeh: And to whom I granted extensive wealth
verses.khattab: and granted him abundant wealth
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and [then] assigned him ample means, abundant and continuous, [generated] from [his] crops, livestock and commerce,
verses.romanUrdu: Bahut sa maal usko diya

verses.saheeh: And children present [with him]
verses.khattab: and children always by his side
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and sons, ten or more, present [by his side], present at social gatherings and whose testimonies are listened to,
verses.romanUrdu: Uske saath hazir rehne waley bete diye

verses.saheeh: And spread [everything] before him, easing [his life].
verses.khattab: and made life very easy for him
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and facilitated, extended, for him greatly, [his] livelihood, duration of life and children.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur uske liye riyasat ki raah hamwaar ki

verses.saheeh: Then he desires that I should add more.
verses.khattab: Yet he is hungry for more
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Still he is eager that I should give [him] more.
verses.romanUrdu: Phir woh tama (greedily desire) rakhta hai ke main usey aur zyada doon

verses.saheeh: No! Indeed, he has been toward Our verses obstinate.
verses.khattab: But no! ˹For˺ he has been truly stubborn with Our revelations
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Nay!, I shall not give him more than that. He is indeed stubborn to Our signs, [to] the Qur'an.
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz nahin woh hamari ayaat se inaath(stubbornly oppose) rakhta hai

verses.saheeh: I will cover him with arduous torment.
verses.khattab: I will make his fate unbearable
verses.jalalayn: ﻿[Soon] I shall burden him with a trying chastisement; alternatively [sa‘ūdan means] a mountain of fire which he will be made to ascend and then fall down from, forever.
verses.romanUrdu: Main to usey ankareeb ek kathin chadhai chadwaunga

verses.saheeh: Indeed, he thought and deliberated.
verses.khattab: for he contemplated and determined ˹a degrading label for the Quran˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Indeed he pondered, what to say about the Qur'an which he heard from the Prophet (s), and decided, this, in his mind.
verses.romanUrdu: Usne socha aur kuch baat banane ki koshish ki

verses.saheeh: So may he be destroyed [for] how he deliberated.
verses.khattab: May he be condemned! How evil was what he determined
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Perish he, may he be cursed and chastised, how he decided!, [perish he] whatever the nature of his decision may have been.
verses.romanUrdu: To khuda ki maar uspar, kaisi baat banane ki koshish ki

verses.saheeh: Then may he be destroyed [for] how he deliberated.
verses.khattab: May he be condemned even more! How evil was what he determined
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Again, perish he, how he decided!
verses.romanUrdu: Haan, khuda ki maar uspar , kaisi baat banane ki koshish ki

verses.saheeh: Then he considered [again];
verses.khattab: Then he re-contemplated ˹in frustration˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Then he contemplated, the faces of his people; or [he contemplated] with what [words] he might cast aspersions upon it.
verses.romanUrdu: Phir(logon ki taraf) dekha

verses.saheeh: Then he frowned and scowled;
verses.khattab: then frowned and scowled
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Then he frowned, he contracted his face and glowered, anguished by what he wanted to say, and scowled, increasing the contracting and the glowering [in his face].
verses.romanUrdu: Phir peshani sukedi aur mooh banaya

verses.saheeh: Then he turned back and was arrogant
verses.khattab: then turned his back ˹on the truth˺ and acted arrogantly
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Then he turned his back, to faith, in disdain, scornful of following the Prophet (s),
verses.romanUrdu: Phir palta aur takabbur mein padh gaya

verses.uthmani: فَقَالَ إِنْ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحْرٌۭ يُؤْثَرُ
verses.indopak: فَقَالَ اِنۡ هٰذَاۤ اِلَّا سِحۡرٌ يُّؤۡثَرُ ۙ
verses.transliteration: faqala in hatha illa sihrun yutharu
verses.saheeh: And said, "This is not but magic imitated [from others].
verses.khattab: saying, “This ˹Quran˺ is nothing but magic from the ancients
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and said, of what he [the Prophet] had brought: ‘This is nothing but handed-down sorcery, learnt from sorcerers;
verses.romanUrdu: Aakhir e kaar bola ke yeh kuch nahin hai magar ek jaadu jo pehle se chala aa raha hai

verses.saheeh: This is not but the word of a human being."
verses.khattab: This is no more than the word of a man.”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿this is nothing but the speech of humans’, similar to what they [the idolaters] had said: ‘It is only a human that is teaching him’ [Q. 16:103].
verses.romanUrdu: Yeh to ek Insani kalaam hai

verses.saheeh: I will drive him into Saqar.
verses.khattab: Soon I will burn him in Hell
verses.jalalayn: ﻿I shall [soon] admit him into Saqar! — Hell.
verses.romanUrdu: Anqareeb main usey dozakh mei jhonk dunga

verses.saheeh: And what can make you know what is Saqar?
verses.khattab: And what will make you realize what Hell is
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And how would you know what is Saqar? — this [interrogative] is intended to emphasise its enormity.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur tum kya jaano ke kya hai woh dozakh

verses.saheeh: It lets nothing remain and leaves nothing [unburned],
verses.khattab: It does not let anyone live or die
verses.jalalayn: ﻿It neither spares nor leaves behind, anything of flesh or nerve, but destroys it [all], after which he is restored to his former state.
verses.romanUrdu: Na baqi rakhey na chodey

verses.saheeh: Blackening the skins.
verses.khattab: scorching the skin
verses.jalalayn: ﻿It burns away the flesh, scorching the surface of skin.
verses.romanUrdu: Khaal(skin) jhulas dene wali

verses.saheeh: Over it are nineteen [angels].
verses.khattab: It is overseen by nineteen ˹keepers˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿There are nineteen [keepers] standing over it, angels, its keepers; a certain disbeliever, who was a mighty stalwart, said, ‘I will avail you seventeen of them, if you avail me [just] two’. God, exalted be He, says:
verses.romanUrdu: Unnis (ninteen) karkoon uspar muqarrar hain

verses.uthmani: وَمَا جَعَلْنَآ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلنَّارِ إِلَّا مَلَٰٓئِكَةًۭ ۙ وَمَا جَعَلْنَا عِدَّتَهُمْ إِلَّا فِتْنَةًۭ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَيَزْدَادَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِيمَٰنًۭا ۙ وَلَا يَرْتَابَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ۙ وَلِيَقُولَ ٱلَّذِينَ فِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌۭ وَٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلًۭا ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ ۚ وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۚ وَمَا هِىَ إِلَّا ذِكْرَىٰ لِلْبَشَرِ
verses.indopak: وَمَا جَعَلۡنَاۤ اَصۡحٰبَ النَّارِ اِلَّا مَلٰٓٮِٕكَةً وَّمَا جَعَلۡنَا عِدَّتَهُمۡ اِلَّا فِتۡنَةً لِّلَّذِيۡنَ كَفَرُوۡا ۙ لِيَسۡتَيۡقِنَ الَّذِيۡنَ اُوۡتُوا الۡكِتٰبَ وَيَزۡدَادَ الَّذِيۡنَ اٰمَنُوۡۤا اِيۡمَانًا وَّلَا يَرۡتَابَ الَّذِيۡنَ اُوۡتُوا الۡكِتٰبَ وَالۡمُؤۡمِنُوۡنَ ۙ وَلِيَقُوۡلَ الَّذِيۡنَ فِىۡ قُلُوۡبِهِمۡ مَّرَضٌ وَّالۡكٰفِرُوۡنَ مَاذَاۤ اَرَادَ اللّٰهُ بِهٰذَا مَثَلًا ؕ كَذٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ اللّٰهُ مَنۡ يَّشَآءُ وَيَهۡدِىۡ مَنۡ يَّشَآءُ ؕ وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ جُنُوۡدَ رَبِّكَ اِلَّا هُوَ ؕ وَمَا هِىَ اِلَّا ذِكۡرٰى لِلۡبَشَرِ
verses.transliteration: wama ja'alna ashaba alnnari illa malaikatan wama ja'alna 'iddatahum illa fitnatan lillatheena kafaroo liyastayqina allatheena ootoo alkitaba wayazdada allatheena amanoo eemanan wala yartaba allatheena ootoo alkitaba waalmuminoona waliyaqoola allatheena fee quloobihim maradun waalkafiroona matha arada allahu bihatha mathalan kathalika yudillu allahu man yashao wayahdee man yashao wama ya'lamu junooda rabbika illa huwa wama hiya illa thikra lilbashari
verses.saheeh: And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels. And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve - that those who were given the Scripture will be convinced and those who have believed will increase in faith and those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt and that those in whose hearts is hypocrisy and the disbelievers will say, "What does Allah intend by this as an example?" Thus does Allah leave astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. And mention of the Fire is not but a reminder to humanity.
verses.khattab: We have appointed only ˹stern˺ angels as wardens of the Fire. And We have made their number only as a test for the disbelievers, so that the People of the Book will be certain, and the believers will increase in faith, and neither the People of the Book nor the believers will have any doubts, and so that those ˹hypocrites˺ with sickness in their hearts and the disbelievers will argue, “What does Allah mean by such a number?” In this way Allah leaves whoever He wills to stray and guides whoever He wills. And none knows the forces of your Lord except He. And this ˹description of Hell˺ is only a reminder to humanity
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And We have appointed only angels as wardens of the Fire, in other words, and so they cannot be withstood as these [disbelievers are wont to] imagine; and We have made their number, so, only as a stumbling-block, a cause for error, for those who disbelieve, when they then say, ‘Why are there nineteen of them?’, so that those who were given the Scripture, namely, the Jews, may be certain, of the sincerity of the Prophet (s) in [saying that] they are nineteen, for this concords with what is in their Scripture; and that those who believe, from among the People of the Scripture, may increase in faith, in affirmation of the truth, given that what the Prophet (s) has said concords with what is in their Scripture, and that those given the Scripture and the believers, [those] other than these [Jews], may not be in doubt, concerning the number of [these] angels, and that those in whose hearts there is a sickness, an uncertainty, [those] in Medina, and the disbelievers, in Mecca, may say, ‘What did God mean by this, number [as a], similitude?’ (mathalan: they referred to it thus [as a mathal] on account of it being a curious matter; in terms of syntax, it [mathalan] is a circumstantial qualifier). Thus, that is, just as the one who rejects this number is led astray and the one who affirms the truth of it is guided, God leads astray whom He will and guides whom He will. And none knows the hosts of your Lord, namely, the angels, [none knows them] in terms of their strength and their assistants, except Him. And it, that is, Saqar, is nothing but a reminder for humans.
verses.romanUrdu: Humne dozakh ke yeh karkoon farishtey banaye hain,aur unki tadaad ko kafiron ke liye fitna bana diya hai, taa-ke ehle kitaab ko yaqeen aa jaye aur iman laney walon ka iman badhey,Aur ehle kitaab aur momineen kisi shakk mein na rahey,aur dil ke bimar aur kuffar yeh kahein ke bhala Allah ka is ajeeb baat se kya matlab ho sakta hai. Is tarah Allah jisey chahta hai gumraah kardeta hai aur jisey chahta hai hidayat baksh deta hai aur tere Rubb ke lashkaron (soldiers) ko khud uske siwa koi nahin janta, aur is dozak ka zikr iske siwa kisi garz ke liye nahin kiya gaya hai ke logon ko issey naseehat ho

verses.saheeh: No! By the moon
verses.khattab: But no! By the moon
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Nay, (kallā: denoting a commencement [of a new sentence], to be understood as alā) by the moon!
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz nahin,kasam hai Chand ki

verses.saheeh: And [by] the night when it departs
verses.khattab: and the night as it retreats
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And by the night when it returns! (if read as idhā dabara), when it comes back after day (a variant reading has idh adbara, meaning ‘when it has receded’).
verses.romanUrdu: Aur Raat ki jabke woh palat-ti hai

verses.saheeh: And [by] the morning when it brightens,
verses.khattab: and the day as it breaks
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And by the dawn when it appears!
verses.romanUrdu: Aur subah ki jabke woh roshan hoti hai

verses.saheeh: Indeed, the Fire is of the greatest [afflictions]
verses.khattab: Surely Hell is one of the mightiest catastrophes—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Verily it, that is, Saqar, is one of the enormities, [one of] the greatest calamities —
verses.romanUrdu: Yeh dozakh bhi badi cheezon mein se ek hai

verses.saheeh: As a warning to humanity -
verses.khattab: a warning to humankind
verses.jalalayn: ﻿a warning (nadhīran is a circumstantial qualifier referring to ihdā, ‘one of’, and it is masculine because it denotes [masculine] ‘adhāb, ‘chastisement’) to [all] humans;
verses.romanUrdu: Insano ke liye darawa

verses.uthmani: لِمَن شَآءَ مِنكُمْ أَن يَتَقَدَّمَ أَوْ يَتَأَخَّرَ
verses.indopak: لِمَنۡ شَآءَ مِنۡكُمۡ اَنۡ يَّتَقَدَّمَ اَوۡ يَتَاَخَّرَ ؕ
verses.transliteration: liman shaa minkum an yataqaddama aw yataakhkhara
verses.saheeh: To whoever wills among you to proceed or stay behind.
verses.khattab: to whichever of you chooses to take the lead or lag behind
verses.jalalayn: ﻿[alike] to those of you who wish (li-man shā’a minkum is a substitution for li’l-bashar, ‘to [all] humans’) to advance, towards good, or towards Paradise by means of faith, or linger behind, in evil, or in Hell because of [their] disbelief.
verses.romanUrdu: Tum mein se har us shaks ke liye darawa jo aagey badhna chahey ya pichey reh jana chahey

verses.saheeh: Every soul, for what it has earned, will be retained
verses.khattab: Every soul will be detained for what it has done
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Every soul is held to ransom by what it earns, [it is] ransomed and requited for its deeds with the Fire,
verses.romanUrdu: Har mutanaffis, apne kasb ke badle rehan hai (hostage to one’s deeds)

verses.saheeh: Except the companions of the right,
verses.khattab: except the people of the right
verses.jalalayn: ﻿except those of the right [hand], namely, the believers who will be saved from it, and [who] will be,
verses.romanUrdu: Dayein bazu walon ke siwa

verses.saheeh: [Who will be] in gardens, questioning each other
verses.khattab: who will be in Gardens, asking one another
verses.jalalayn: ﻿in gardens, questioning one another,
verses.romanUrdu: Jo jannaton mein hongey, wahan woh

verses.saheeh: About the criminals,
verses.khattab: about the wicked ˹who will then be asked˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿about the guilty, and their predicament; and they will say to them, after all those who believed in the One God (muwahhidūn) are brought out of the Fire:
verses.romanUrdu: Mujrimon se puchenge

verses.saheeh: [And asking them], "What put you into Saqar?"
verses.khattab: “What has landed you in Hell?”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿‘What has landed you in, [what has] made you enter, Saqar?’
verses.romanUrdu: Tumhein kya cheez dozakh mein le gayi

verses.saheeh: They will say, "We were not of those who prayed,
verses.khattab: They will reply, “We were not of those who prayed
verses.jalalayn: ﻿They will say, ‘We were not of those who prayed.
verses.romanUrdu: woh kahenge “hum namaz padne walon mein se na thay

verses.saheeh: Nor did we used to feed the poor.
verses.khattab: nor did we feed the poor
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Nor did we [ever] feed the needy.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur miskeen ko khana nahin khilate thay

verses.saheeh: And we used to enter into vain discourse with those who engaged [in it],
verses.khattab: We used to indulge ˹in falsehood˺ along with others
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And we used to delve, into falsehood, along with those who delved,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur haqq ke khilaf batein banane walon ke saath milkar hum bhi batein banane lagte thay

verses.saheeh: And we used to deny the Day of Recompense
verses.khattab: and deny the Day of Judgment
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and we used to deny the Day of Judgement, [the Day] of Resurrection and Requital,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur roz-e-jaza ko jhoot karar dete thay

verses.saheeh: Until there came to us the certainty."
verses.khattab: until the inevitable came to us.”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿until [finally] the inevitable came to us’ — death.
verses.romanUrdu: Yahan tak ke humein us yaqeeni cheez se saabqa pesh aa gaya”

verses.saheeh: So there will not benefit them the intercession of [any] intercessors.
verses.khattab: So the pleas of intercessors will be of no benefit to them
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Thus the intercession of the intercessors, from among the angels, the prophets and the righteous, will not avail them, in other words, there will be no intercession for them.
verses.romanUrdu: Us waqt sifarish karne walon ki sifarish unke kisi kaam na ayegi

verses.saheeh: Then what is [the matter] with them that they are, from the reminder, turning away
verses.khattab: Now, what is the matter with them that they are turning away from the reminder
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So what (fa-mā: the subject) is wrong with them (lahum: the predicate thereof, semantically connected to an omitted clause, the person of which has been transposed onto it) that they turn away (mu‘ridīna is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the [suffixed] pronoun [in lahum, ‘them’]) from the Reminder — in other words, ‘what has happened to them that they have turned away from admonition’ —
verses.romanUrdu: Aakhir in logon ko kya ho gaya hai ke yeh is nasihat se mooh moad rahey hain

verses.saheeh: As if they were alarmed donkeys
verses.khattab: as if they were spooked zebras
verses.jalalayn: ﻿as if they were wild asses
verses.romanUrdu: Goya yeh jungli gadhey hain

verses.saheeh: Fleeing from a lion?
verses.khattab: fleeing from a lion
verses.jalalayn: ﻿fleeing from a lion?, that is to say, fleeing from it with absolute fright.
verses.romanUrdu: Jo Sher se darr kar bhaag padey hain

verses.uthmani: بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِئٍۢ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُؤْتَىٰ صُحُفًۭا مُّنَشَّرَةًۭ
verses.indopak: بَلۡ يُرِيۡدُ كُلُّ امۡرِىٴٍ مِّنۡهُمۡ اَنۡ يُّؤۡتٰى صُحُفًا مُّنَشَّرَةً ۙ
verses.transliteration: bal yureedu kullu imriin minhum an yuta suhufan munashsharatan
verses.saheeh: Rather, every person among them desires that he would be given scriptures spread about.
verses.khattab: In fact, each one of them wishes to be given a ˹personal˺ letter ˹from Allah˺ for all ˹to read˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Nay, but everyone of them desires to be given unrolled scrolls, from God, exalted be He, [enjoining them] to follow the Prophet (s), as they said [before], ‘And [even then] we will not believe your ascension until you bring down for us a book that we may read’ [Q. 17:93].
verses.romanUrdu: Balke inmein se to har ek yeh chahta hai ke uske naam khule khat (scroll/scripture) bhejey jaye

verses.saheeh: No! But they do not fear the Hereafter.
verses.khattab: But no! In fact, they do not fear the Hereafter
verses.jalalayn: ﻿No indeed! (kallā: a deterrent of what they desire). Rather they do not fear the Hereafter, that is, the chastisement thereof.
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz nahin, Asal baat yeh hai ke yeh aakhirat ka khauf nahin rakhtey

verses.saheeh: No! Indeed, the Qur'an is a reminder
verses.khattab: Enough! Surely this ˹Quran˺ is a reminder
verses.jalalayn: ﻿No indeed! (kallā: a commencement [of a new sentence]) Assuredly it, that is, the Qur'an, is a Reminder, an admonition.
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz nahin,yeh to ek nasihat hai

verses.saheeh: Then whoever wills will remember it.
verses.khattab: So let whoever wills be mindful of it
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So whoever wills shall remember it, he shall read it and be admonished by it.
verses.romanUrdu: Ab jiska jee chahey issey sabaq hasil karle

verses.uthmani: وَمَا يَذْكُرُونَ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ ۚ هُوَ أَهْلُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ وَأَهْلُ ٱلْمَغْفِرَةِ
verses.indopak: وَمَا يَذۡكُرُوۡنَ اِلَّاۤ اَنۡ يَّشَآءَ اللّٰهُ ؕ هُوَ اَهۡلُ التَّقۡوٰى وَاَهۡلُ الۡمَغۡفِرَةِ
verses.transliteration: wama yathkuroona illa an yashaa allahu huwa ahlu alttaqwa waahlu almaghfirati
verses.saheeh: And they will not remember except that Allah wills. He is worthy of fear and adequate for [granting] forgiveness.
verses.khattab: But they cannot do so unless Allah wills. He ˹alone˺ is worthy to be feared and entitled to forgive
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And they will not remember (yadhkurūna or [read second person plural] tadhkurūna) unless God wills [it]. He is [the One] worthy of [your] fear, and [the One] worthy to forgive, by forgiving those who fear Him.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur yeh koi sabaq hasil na karengey illa yeh ke Allah hi aisa chahey woh iska haqdar hai ke ussey taqwa kiya jaye aur woh iska ehal hai ke (taqwa karne walon ko) baksh de
